structure: Part 14 read the whole repo-root `fit/` folder of repos/trade-imports-plants-frontend in full, which holds exactly five files (confirmed with `find fit -type f`): `journey-smoke.fit.spec.js` (225 lines), `high-risk-plants-journey.js` (1,596 lines), `set-base.js` (125 lines), `sign-in.js` (9 lines) and `seed-fields.js` (10 lines). `journey-smoke.fit.spec.js` holds four `test(...)` declarations, two of them in loops, giving nine test instances: one smoke test per shape of the flow's `happy-path.json` fixture (five shapes - warePotatoes, warePotatoesLate, seedPotatoes, plantsForPlanting, woodWithoutBark), each walking the whole journey from the dashboard to confirmation and asserting every step's URL and trail; one Back test per shape in `BACK_TARGETS_BY_PAGE_ON_FORWARD_WALK` (warePotatoes, woodWithoutBark); and two standalone Back tests on the seed-potato walk. The spec reads its answers from the fixture (another part's file; read here only to say what the walk enters and asserts) and every label, button and message from the features' own `copy/copy.en.js` and `shared/copy.en.js`. `high-risk-plants-journey.js` is the page-by-page harness every fit spec in the repo drives the journey with: walk constants (POTATO_WALK, the review URLs and the Change-link trail), save-control and Back locators, the whole dashboard-to-confirmation walk as composable helpers (startNotification, chooseCommodityType, addCommodityLine, saveOrigin, startPotatoNotification, startPotatoNotificationAtContact, completePotatoNotification, openDeclaration, submitDeclarationFromCheckAnswers, the wood variants and startNotificationAtOverview/startNotificationAtOrigin), the shared axe gate, the no-JavaScript reopener, the type-ahead chooser, and three shared test factories that declare whole suites for every address picker (describeAddressPicker, describeSubmittedSearchPicker) and every MOJ date picker (describeDatePickerLook). `set-base.js`, `sign-in.js` and `seed-fields.js` are the set-up mechanisms: the set's mount prefix and the trail-aware URL matchers, the stub sign-in, and the resolution of relative fixture dates. Covered: the four smoke tests and their nine instances; the journey walked page by page in order (commodity-type, commodities/details, commodities, origin, arrival-status, arrival-details, destinations/select, consignors/select, identification-numbers, consignment/contact/select, notification-view, declaration, confirmation) with the answers entered and the headings, labels and messages asserted; the commodity-type and arrival-status branches and the late branch; the shared picker, date-picker, save-control, axe and no-JavaScript suites the harness declares; and the three set-up files as mechanism claims. Amend and copy are a gap: the harness carries no helper for either.

claims.statement: A signed-in trader can take a high-risk plants notification from the dashboard through to confirmation, and this is proven for five use cases: ware potatoes from Spain notified before arrival, ware potatoes from Portugal notified after arrival, seed potatoes from the Netherlands, spruce (Picea) from Germany with species and EPPO code, and conifer wood without bark from Italy with phytosanitary treatments.
claims.quote:
for (const [name, shape] of Object.entries(happyPaths)) {
  test(`${name}: ${shape.useCase} reaches confirmation`, async ({ page }) => {
claims.note: The five useCase strings are quoted verbatim from the fixture: "Ware potatoes from Spain, notified before arrival", "Ware potatoes from Portugal, notified after arrival", "Seed potatoes from the Netherlands", "Spruce (Picea) from Germany, with species and EPPO code", "Conifer wood without bark from Italy, with phytosanitary treatments". The fixture itself belongs to the flow part; it is read here only to say what the smoke walk enters and proves.

claims.statement: On the commodities list, the arrival details, the identification numbers and the consignment contact pages, Back opens the page the trader pressed Save and continue on, and this is proven for a ware-potato walk and a wood walk.

On a ware-potato notification, Back goes from the commodities list to commodity-type, from the arrival details to origin, from the identification numbers to the place of destination picker, and from the consignment contact to the identification numbers.

On a wood-without-bark notification, Back goes from the arrival details to the arrival status question and from the identification numbers to the consignor picker, where a potato notification goes to origin and to the place of destination picker, so Back follows the branch the commodity type opened.
